title: Japan's Shimizu Invests in Noble Machines to Develop Humanoid Robots for Construction
machine_does: Japanese builder Shimizu invests (amount not disclosed) in Noble Machines of Sunnyvale, California, to build MOBY humanoid robots that move materials and patrol construction sites; computer simulations start by end of 2026, tests on real sites from spring 2027.
why_it_matters: A big construction firm is betting humanoids can fill the labor gap of an aging workforce.
date_checked: AI Insider page metadata datePublished 2026-10-16T10:31Z; Shimizu's own release (Google News pubDate 2026-10-16T03:00Z, noon JST 16 Oct) is a few hours before the window start, so first English coverage is inside the window; not in the 12-16 Oct pools; no earlier 14-day coverage found.

title: Large-scale iontronic skins with neural-hierarchical processing architecture (NI-skin: artificial skin with 10,000+ touch sensors for humanoid robots)
machine_does: Researchers at Southern University of Science and Technology (Shenzhen) built an artificial skin with more than 10,000 touch sensors (1,110 per square centimetre) that reads all sensors at once through one channel, designed to give humanoid robots a human-like sense of touch.
why_it_matters: Touch is a main missing sense for robot hands and bodies; a skin that scales to a whole humanoid is a step toward robots that handle things safely.
date_checked: Nature page metadata dc.date and citation_online_date 2026-10-16 (published 16 Oct); Bioengineer.org write-up 2026-10-17T01:5xZ read in full; no coverage found before 16 Oct. Nature page carries a date only, not a time.

title: Unitree Releases UniUni Swarm Control Software, Free for Its Users, Starting With H2 and G1
machine_does: Unitree launched UniUni, a free Windows and macOS app that lets one person draw paths, arrange timelines, sync motion to music and watch a whole fleet of its H2 and G1 humanoid robots, with a one-tap emergency stop.
why_it_matters: Controlling many humanoids at once, for shows and later for work, gets much easier and costs nothing extra for Unitree owners.
date_checked: Pandaily page metadata shows 2026-10-17T01:45:00Z (Google News pubDate 02:15Z); only Pandaily found in a 14-day search, so no earlier coverage. Page body is script-rendered, so the description line and headline were read, not the full text.

title: Can a $55,000 robot load the dishwasher? Inside my afternoon with two humanoid housekeepers
machine_does: MarketWatch reporter spends an afternoon testing two humanoid home robots that cost $55,000 and up, to see if they can load a dishwasher and do other housework.
why_it_matters: A first hands-on test of what home humanoids can really do at today's prices.

title: Pune-Based Muks Robotics Secures ISRO Project to Develop SPACEO Prime, an Indian Humanoid Space Worker
machine_does: India's space agency ISRO gave Muks Robotics of Pune a project to develop SPACEO Prime, described as India's first humanoid space worker to assist astronauts in hazardous tasks (company press release, no budget or date given).
why_it_matters: India is starting a humanoid for space work, a sign the humanoid race now reaches space programs.
date_checked: Tribune page datePublished 2026-10-16T15:56:32+05:30 (=10:26Z); only this outlet in a 14-day search; paid-press-release style text read in full.

title: Two humanoid robots team up to play table tennis doubles, rally for over 10 shots
machine_does: Researchers from the University of Hong Kong, Shanghai Innovation Institute, Archon Robotics and Nvidia built PingpongDuo, software that lets two humanoid robots play table tennis doubles, taking turns to hit and moving out of each other's way, with rallies of more than 10 shots.
why_it_matters: Two robots sharing a small space and coordinating in real time is a hard step toward robot teams; also a fun clip.
date_checked: Interesting Engineering page datePublished 2026-10-16T13:44:16Z, read in full; the research paper's own posting date was not found, only this outlet in a 30-day search.

title: A Humanoid Robot Now Speaks Quechua, Thanks to Fine-Tuned Neural Speech Synthesis
source: Bioengineer.org (study in Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
machine_does: Researchers at Universidad Senor de Sipan in Peru taught a UBTech Walker Tienkung humanoid to speak Southern Quechua, spoken by more than 10 million people, by training a speech model on 30.5 hours of Quechua and running it on the robot itself.
why_it_matters: Robots that speak an Indigenous language show humanoids need not serve only English and Chinese speakers.
date_checked: Bioengineer.org page metadata 2026-10-17 02:52 BST (=01:52Z), read in full; the Frontiers paper's own date was not confirmed; only this outlet found in a 14-day search.

title: Rareview Capital and Tuttle Capital Management Launch Humanoid Robotics ETF HOID
machine_does: A new actively managed exchange-traded fund, HOID, launched on 16 Oct to invest in companies that make humanoid robots and the AI, chips, sensors, actuators and batteries behind them.
why_it_matters: Humanoid robots now have their own fund for ordinary investors, a sign of money flowing into the field.
date_checked: PR Newswire release dated 'Las Vegas, Oct. 16, 2026', page datePublished 2026-10-16T07:02-04:00 (=11:02Z), read in full; no earlier coverage.

title: SoftBank Is Said to Weigh Buying Top US Security Firm Allied
machine_does: SoftBank Group is weighing a purchase of Allied Universal, the largest private security company in the US (about $18 billion equity, close to $30 billion with debt), because CEO Masayoshi Son sees security as a field where AI robots could replace some human guards; talks are early and nothing is decided.
why_it_matters: A buyer of Son's size would give security robots a huge ready customer base, with real jobs and money at stake.
date_checked: Bloomberg Google News pubDate 2026-10-16T19:11Z, Reuters 21:22Z, Yahoo Finance/Investing.com 19:02-19:29Z; details read in the BigGo Finance summary (datePublished 2026-10-16T20:35Z) because Bloomberg and Yahoo pages are blocked to curl; the 12-16 Oct pools hold only SoftBank junk-bond and Son interview items, not this.

machine_does: Japan is using AI detection, four-legged robot dogs and drones that spray pepper spray to keep bears away from people as attacks rise (headline and URL date only; the article is behind the paywall).
why_it_matters: A clear case of robots protecting people from wild animals, a story that travels well across countries.

title: China completes world's third robotic arm-assisted heart transplant
machine_does: Surgeons at the First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University used robotic arms through small chest cuts to replace a 67-year-old man's heart on 5 Oct, the first such operation in China and the third in the world; remote operation is a possible next step.
why_it_matters: Robot-assisted transplants avoid cutting the breastbone, which may make the riskiest heart surgery safer for frail patients.
date_checked: China Daily page metadata 'Updated 2026-10-16 17:17 (China)' = 09:17Z, read in full; the operation was 5 Oct but this is its first report (only China Daily and a copy of it found in a 14-day search).

title: A retired Penn professor has been blocking Uber Eats robots for months. This week, she got arrested for it
machine_does: A 78-year-old retired University of Pennsylvania professor, Carolyn Marvin, was arrested on Wed 14 Oct for disorderly conduct after standing in the way of an Uber Eats sidewalk delivery robot in Center City Philadelphia, a protest against robots replacing human delivery workers.
why_it_matters: The first arrest tied to a protest against delivery robots, carried by many outlets, shows the public pushback against robots taking jobs.
date_checked: PhillyVoice page datePublished 2026-10-16T13:17:24-04:00 (=17:17Z), read in full; the arrest was Wed 14 Oct and the first local report (6abc) was 15 Oct 21:32Z, but about ten outlets (Washington Times, Yahoo, Inc., Dexerto, BroBible, Hoodline and others) carried it on 16 Oct inside the window; it is not in the 12-16 Oct pools (they hold only the Chicago delivery-robot lawsuits).
